title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Fundamentals tell you what to own; the Stage 2 tape tells you when institutional capital is quietly accumulating it without forcing you to chase an extended breakout.

book_paragraphs: Even the finest business in the world can hand you a painful 20% drawdown if you buy it in the wrong stage of the market cycle. That is why we always check the tape before committing capital. As of the verified November 13, 2026 close, JPMorgan Chase's chart tells a clear story of patience: while the broader S&P 500 is digesting six distribution days in a short-term correction, JPM sits in Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) at $346.19.

Look closely at the moving averages. JPM closed at $346.19 (+0.98% on light 4.20M volume, 0.63x average), sitting +1.65% above its 10-week EMA ($340.58) and +1.70% above a flat-to-falling 50-day moving average ($340.42, down from $348.45 three weeks ago). Meanwhile, its rising 30-week moving average sits below at $335.05 and its 200-day moving average at $324.86, with daily RSI at 56.12 and 63-day relative strength at -1.72%.

In plain English, JPM is consolidating right under Pivot R1 ($346.84) resistance rather than breaking out on heavy institutional volume. Buying at $346.19 risks $23.68 per share (-6.84%) down to our $322.51 invalidation stop for $41.90 of Base Case upside (+12.10%)—a modest 1.77-to-1 ratio. Waiting for a pullback into the $326.16–$335.05 support zone lifts that reward-to-risk to 4.23-to-1.

On the options side, 26.5% implied volatility sits slightly below 28.0% 20-day realized volatility. However, a single September 2027 $315 LEAPS Call costs roughly $4,933—which exceeds our current $3,818.88 US cash reserve. That is another reason to stay patient and stage common-equity tranches only if JPM tests $326.16–$335.05.

book_subsections.title: Reading Institutional Footprints: Why Light-Volume Bounces Demand Patience
paragraphs: Here is a simple tape-reading habit that will save you from countless bad trades: whenever a stock bounces inside a Stage 3 consolidation, look at the volume bar before you celebrate. On November 13, 2026, JPM rose 0.98% to $346.19 on just 4.20 million shares—0.63x its 20-day average.

Light-volume rallies into Pivot R1 ($346.84) resistance while the 50-day moving average ($340.42) is sloping flat-to-down rarely sustain immediate breakouts during a broader market Correction. That is why we wait for a test of the $326.16–$335.05 shelf, or a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above $346.84.

Think of it like watching a sprinter catch their breath at the top of a hill: JPMorgan Chase's long-term 200-day moving average ($324.86) and 30-week moving average ($335.05) are still rising underneath, confirming the primary institutional foundation is intact. Yet until the 50-day moving average stops flattening and volume expands above 1.2x average on a move through $346.84, letting the stock come to your $326.16–$335.05 price zone is the highest-probability play.

Remember also what the broader market regime is telling us: with the S&P 500 in a Correction and six distribution days on the tape, even strong universal banks rarely launch into sustained breakouts without first shaking out late buyers. Letting JPMorgan test its 30-week moving average on quiet volume puts institutional probability firmly on your side.

book_subsections.title: Why Sizing Constraints Keep Us Out of Premature LEAPS
paragraphs: Most retail traders lose money in options because they stretch their account cash to buy contracts that exceed their natural risk budget. On November 13, 2026, JPM's 30-day implied volatility sits at 26.5%—slightly below 28.0% realized volatility—making the September 17, 2027 $315 Call reasonably priced on volatility.

Yet at ~$49.33 per share ($4,933 total per contract), one contract costs more than our entire $3,818.88 US cash balance. Discipline means matching the vehicle to both the tape and the wallet: hold cash until JPM tests $326.16–$335.05, then stage common shares with a $322.51 weekly-close stop.

Keep those three levels marked clearly on your weekly chart: $326.16–$335.05 as the primary accumulation shelf where Pivot S1 meets the rising 30-week moving average, $346.84 as the Pivot R1 breakout confirmation on expanding volume, and $322.51 as your non-negotiable weekly-close invalidation stop below the 200-day moving average ($324.86). If JPM breaks below $322.51 on a weekly close, cancel pending buy orders immediately and preserve cash.
